comparisons.peer_summary: Multiple lawsuits alleging LIBOR manipulation by the Corporation, BANA, and other banks remain pending in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, with motions for summary judgment currently pending for remaining claims involving individual and class plaintiffs.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup (C) and Bank of America (BAC) are defendants in the specific multi-district litigation regarding the manipulation of USD LIBOR before the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. While Citigroup discloses that putative class actions and individual actions have been dismissed or settled with only surviving claims remaining against it, Bank of America states that all remaining cases are still pending with motions for summary judgment currently outstanding for both individual and class plaintiffs.

sentences.text: Citigroup and Citibank, along with other U.S. Dollar (USD) LIBOR panel banks, are defendants in a multi-district litigation proceeding before the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York captioned IN RE LIBOR-BASED FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS ANTITRUST LITIGATION.
The putative class actions and certain of the individual actions have been dismissed as to Citigroup and Citibank based on pretrial rulings or following settlements.
Beginning in 2011, several individual and putative class actions were filed against the Corporation, BANA, and certain Merrill Lynch entities, as well as other banks on the U.S. Dollar LIBOR panel.

Defendants' motion for summary judgment is pending on all remaining claims, brought by individual plaintiffs and one class of plaintiffs who purchased over-the-counter instruments incorporating LIBOR.

comparisons.peer_topic: Variable Rate Demand Obligations Antitrust Litigation Status
comparisons.peer_summary: GS&Co. is a defendant in a consolidated putative class action alleging a conspiracy to manipulate the market for variable rate demand obligations (VRDOs) through federal antitrust and state law claims. While Group Inc. was dismissed in 2019 and various state law and fiduciary duty claims against GS&Co. were dismissed by the district court in 2020 and 2022, the federal antitrust claims remain active as the proceedings are stayed pending an interlocutory appeal of the 2023 class certification grant by the Second Circuit.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup (C) and Goldman Sachs (GS) are named as defendants in antitrust litigation involving alleged manipulation of financial benchmarks, with both facing proceedings in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. However, the subject matter differs: Citigroup's litigation concerns USD LIBOR manipulation under the Sherman Act and state law, whereas Goldman Sachs is defending against consolidated putative class actions alleging a conspiracy to manipulate the market for Variable Rate Demand Obligations (VRDOs) through federal antitrust claims. Additionally, GS specifically notes its proceedings are stayed pending an interlocutory appeal, whereas C notes surviving claims assert damages for USD LIBOR suppression.

sentences.text: Citigroup and Citibank, along with other U.S. Dollar (USD) LIBOR panel banks, are defendants in a multi-district litigation proceeding before the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York captioned IN RE LIBOR-BASED FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS ANTITRUST LITIGATION.
Plaintiffs with surviving claims against Citigroup and Citibank assert claims under the Sherman Act and state law based on allegations that defendants suppressed or otherwise manipulated USD LIBOR.

The consolidated amended complaint, filed on May 31, 2019, generally asserts claims under federal antitrust law and state common law in connection with an alleged conspiracy among the defendants to manipulate the market for VRDOs.
On February 5, 2024, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit granted the defendants' petition seeking interlocutory review of the district court's grant of class certification.

comparisons.peer_summary: The monetary relief class action settled for ~$6.2 billion with $700 million returned to defendants; a separate injunctive class action saw preliminary approval denied in June 2024, while individual actions by opting merchants have mostly settled representing over 70% of sales volume. Ongoing matters include a Swiss EURIBOR investigation and a U.S. Court of Appeals affirmation of a dismissal in an antitrust lawsuit; the Firm has resolved all non-U.S. dollar LIBOR actions and obtained dismissals or moved for summary judgment in remaining U.S. dollar LIBOR cases.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup (C) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) face litigation related to U.S. dollar LIBOR administration and manipulation. JPMorgan provides more granular status updates, noting that while some class actions have settled (e.g., monetary relief class action settled for ~$6.2 billion) or been dismissed (individual plaintiff antitrust claims dismissed in October 2023 and affirmed on appeal), other actions remain pending. Citigroup similarly describes a landscape where many actions were dismissed or settled, but surviving plaintiffs continue to assert Sherman Act and state law claims seeking compensatory damages for USD LIBOR manipulation.

sentences.text: Citigroup and Citibank, along with other U.S. Dollar (USD) LIBOR panel banks, are defendants in a multi-district litigation proceeding before the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York captioned IN RE LIBOR-BASED FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS ANTITRUST LITIGATION.
The putative class actions and certain of the individual actions have been dismissed as to Citigroup and Citibank based on pretrial rulings or following settlements.
In September 2018, the parties settled the class action seeking monetary relief, with the defendants collectively contributing approximately $6.2 billion.

In addition, a lawsuit filed by a group of individual plaintiffs asserting antitrust claims, alleging that the Firm and other defendants were engaged in an unlawful agreement to set U.S. dollar LIBOR and conspired to monopolize the market for LIBOR-based consumer loans and credit cards was dismissed in October 2023 and affirmed on appeal by the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit in December 2024.
